record.paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
record.original_question: What mechanism explains the surprisingly low proton-to-pion ratio at the LHC despite fits with a reduced chemical freeze-out temperature, and can baryon final-state annihilation or late baryon freeze-out be distinguished from other explanations without creating tension with hyperon abundances and resonance-ratio constraints?

evidence.quote: Another hint of non-equilibrium may be the surprisingly low p/π-ratio at LHC; despite pulling down by almost 10 MeV the chemical freeze-out temperature compared to pre-LHC fits - which leads to a slight tension with some Hyperon abundances which seem to prefer the original Tchem - the p/π-ratio remains well below most predictions.
Amongst a number of possible explanations, baryon final state annihilation (i.e. late baryon freeze-out) is a leading but not the only contender.

Resonance ratios are therefore a sensitive measure of the final state interaction taking place after hadronisation; they are well described by transport codes (EPOS, URQMD) and consequently strongly disfavour models with a single (Tchem=Tkin) chemical and kinetic freeze-out.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions at LHC energies (Pb–Pb at center-of-mass energies of a few TeV per nucleon pair), modeled within the statistical/thermal hadronization framework with chemical freeze-out temperature T_chem and kinetic freeze-out temperature T_kin, possibly followed by a hadronic rescattering phase described by transport models (e.g., URQMD, EPOS).

Empirical observations to be explained simultaneously:
(i) The integrated proton-to-pion yield ratio p/π measured in central Pb–Pb collisions lies well below predictions of standard equilibrium thermal fits, even after lowering T_chem by roughly 10 MeV relative to pre-LHC values.
(ii) Lowering T_chem by this amount creates tension with measured hyperon (Λ, Ξ, Ω) abundances, which prefer a higher T_chem closer to the pre-LHC value.
(iii) Measured short-lived resonance-to-stable-particle yield ratios (e.g., K*/K, ρ/π, Λ*/Λ) are well reproduced by hadronic transport simulations including post-hadronization rescattering, and disfavor scenarios in which chemical and kinetic freeze-out coincide (T_chem = T_kin).

Problem: Identify a hadronic-phase mechanism — for instance, baryon–antibaryon final-state annihilation (BB̄ → multi-meson) producing late effective baryon freeze-out — that quantitatively reproduces the suppressed p/π ratio, while remaining simultaneously consistent with measured hyperon abundances and with the resonance-ratio constraints (i)–(iii). Determine whether such a mechanism can be unambiguously distinguished from alternative explanations (e.g., non-equilibrium chemistry, flavor-dependent freeze-out, or modified hadron spectra) by existing or future observables.
artifact.status_search_result: The anomalously low p/π ratio at the LHC remains an actively discussed puzzle. Baryon–antibaryon annihilation in the hadronic phase (as implemented in UrQMD/EPOS afterburners) is a leading but not unique explanation, and tensions with hyperon yields and resonance-ratio constraints persist. Recent LHC measurements (e.g., strange-baryon studies in 2024–2025) continue to probe these issues without delivering a fully unique mechanistic resolution.

status_evidence.title: First observation of strange baryon enhancement with effective energy in pp collisions at the LHC
status_evidence.snippet: Recent LHC measurements continue to investigate baryon-to-meson production ratios, indicating that the interpretation of strange and non-strange baryon yields is still under active study.
status_evidence.claim: Baryon production ratios at the LHC remain an active research topic without a settled single mechanism.
